newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister attacks car incentive scheme.
newsitem.headline: French minister attacks car incentive scheme.

text.p: French junior industry minister Christian Pierret on Thursday attacked a car incentive scheme set up by the previous conservative government for artificially boosting sales and putting an additional burden on the 1997 budget.

"We must not do what Mr Balladur and Juppe did, that is an incentive scheme that boosts sales for a while and then depresses them... this is very costly for public finances," Pierret told the RTL radio.

He said the new Socialist government was faced with the challenge of finding ways to finance some 500 million francs stemming from the car incentive scheme set up by former Prime Minister Alain Juppe.

"The Juppe government is leaving 500 million francs in unfinanced Juppe scheme that were not included in the 1997 budget. We have to find the means to meet the commitments taken by Mr Juppe," he said.
Asked if the Socialist government would consider cutting value added tax on cars to help beef up sales, Pierret said:

"One must look at the state of public finances. I don't believe we can play with VAT rates according to the situation of such and such sector. We must have a long-term vision of the future of the car industry."
French car sales fell 30.7 percent to 93,212 units in June from 134,489 a year earlier, the worst June performance since 1962.
The CCFA carmaker association said the June figures showed demand had not recovered from the after-effects of a state rebate which ran out last September.
